basis: Migne prints his own reference to Genesis 16:7-12 inside this answer, which asks 'Inter. 172. Quomodo manus omnium contra Ismaelem, et manus ejus contra omnes (Gen. XVI,'. The extent is that reference and nothing wider.
date_basis: The dedicatory letter addresses Sigewulf, Alcuin's pupil and his successor at Tours, and says the questions are ones Sigewulf had put to him over a long acquaintance and are now gathered. Alcuin was abbot of Tours from 796 until his death in 804. The work is conventionally placed in the Tours years and near their beginning; the range records that and no more. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1851 printing, and it is not the seventh century the wiki header gives, which is a century out.
text: Inter. 172. Quomodo manus omnium contra Ismaelem, et manus ejus contra omnes (Gen. XVI, 7, 12)?-- Resp. Invenit [enim] angelus Domini Agar super fontem aquae in deserto ad fontem in via Assur, quae per eremum ducit ad Aegyptum, [ire festinabat]: Et vocavit nomen ejus Ismael, quia exaudivit Dominus humilitatem [ejus] (Ismael interpretatur exauditio Domini [ Ms., Dei]): Hic erit ferus homo, manus ejus super omnes, et manus omnium super eum, et contra faciem omnium fratrum suorum habitabit. Significat autem semen ejus habitaturum in eremo, id est, Sarracenos vagos, incertisque sedibus, qui universas gentes, quibus desertum ex latere jungitur, incursant et impugnant, [et impugnantur ab omnibus].
